question: What share of cervical carcinomas does ESMO describe as HPV-independent?
explanation: The vast majority are HPV-associated, whereas 10–15% are HPV-independent [1].
sourceArticle: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up

question: Squamous-cell carcinoma accounts for approximately:
explanation: Squamous-cell carcinoma accounts for 70–80% and adenocarcinoma for 20–25% [1].
sourceArticle: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up

question: When does ESMO recommend PD-L1 combined positive score?

options.A: When it has therapeutic implications, level [I, A]
options.C: Only after recurrence in the brain

correctAnswerText: When it has therapeutic implications, level [I, A]
explanation: Assessing PD-L1 expression by combined positive score is recommended when it has therapeutic implications, graded [I, A] [1].
sourceArticle: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up

question: How should a retrieved lymph node be submitted?

options.A: The whole node in 2 mm sections [III, A]
options.D: It should be discarded if under 1 cm

correctAnswerText: The whole node in 2 mm sections [III, A]
explanation: Total submission of the lymph node in 2 mm sections into paraffin blocks is recommended [III, A] [1].
sourceArticle: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up

question: PET-CT sensitivity for para-aortic nodes in locally advanced disease is:
explanation: Sensitivity for para-aortic nodes is 0.40 (95% CI 0.18–0.66) and specificity 0.93 (0.91–0.95). Pelvic-node sensitivity is higher, 0.88, but with a wide confidence interval [1].
sourceArticle: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up
